title: The Oath of the Weeping Wood Revisited
premise: Orsen Kavanagh, a royal food-taster who poisons himself in small doses to stay alive, secretly keeps the ledgers of the Weeping Wood—a guild that trades in impossible things: borrowed years, stolen names, grief bottled and sold. When a dying courier presses a map of the old covenant between the human realm and the Wood into Orsen's hands, they become the last living witness to a betrayal that broke the pact decades ago, and every faction that profited from its breaking wants them silenced. Hunted by the crown's inquisitor, pursued by the guild's exiled founder, and shadowed by a Wood that remembers everything Orsen has tried to forget, they must choose between loyalty to the guild that raised them and the truth that could restore—or destroy—the covenant. In the end, Orsen rebinds the realms not with an oath spoken aloud but with their own ledger of debts, paying the final entry with their immunity itself, so that the Wood weeps for the first time in living memory.
about_author: E. M. Villalobos is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing broken contracts and unfulfilled wills in a coastal provincial records office. They write fantasy about people who keep accounts—of money, of promises, of wounds—and live somewhere damp with two cats named after failed treaties.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. We meet Orsen mid-service at the royal table, swallowing a suspect dish and surviving it, then slipping away to update the Weeping Wood's ledgers in a cellar shrine. The chapter establishes their double life: invisible servant by day, keeper of impossible debts by night. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness; Orsen believes invisibility is safety.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Dripping Gate
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. A dying courier staggers into the guild's hidden entrance, presses a bloodstained map of the old covenant into Orsen's hands, and dies naming Orsen as 'the one who counts.' The map shows a route through the Wood to the Broken Stone where the oath was sworn. Emotional beat: terror and reluctant responsibility; the first crack in Orsen's invisibility.

chapters.title: What the Ledgers Omit
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Searching the guild archives, Orsen discovers pages razored out of the covenant's founding record—and realizes the guild's matriarch, Sable Vey, was present when it broke. Meanwhile the royal inquisitor Dame Corvane begins asking why a food-taster visits cellars. Emotional beat: dawning suspicion that everything Orsen trusted was built on an erasure.

chapters.title: The Price of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: POV alternating between Orsen and Dame Corvane. Corvane interrogates palace staff while Orsen flees into the city's underside, trading a favor with a fence of bottled grief to learn the map's first waypoint. The Wood itself begins appearing in reflections where it shouldn't be. Emotional beat: hunted claustrophobia; the city turning unfamiliar.

chapters.title: Sable Vey's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Confronting Sable Vey, Orsen learns the truth: the guild's founders broke the covenant deliberately, selling the realms' shared memory to buy the guild's power—and Sable has been keeping Orsen close all these years because tasters' blood can reseal oaths. Emotional beat: betrayal crystallizing; loyalty and truth pull apart.

chapters.title: Into the Weeping Wood
chapters.summary: POV Orsen, with Corvane closing behind. Orsen crosses into the Wood, where trees bleed sap that replays memories of anyone who touches them. Orsen relives their own buried past—the family sold to the guild as collateral—and understands why they were chosen. Emotional beat: grief made physical; the map begins rewriting itself as the Wood tests them.

chapters.title: The Exile Who Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Deep in the Wood, Orsen finds Idris, the guild's exiled founder, kept alive by the covenant's residue and rotting with guilt. Idris reveals the final requirement: the oath must be reforged with a willing payment, not a coerced one—and offers to take Orsen's place if Orsen kills him. Emotional beat: strange compassion for an enemy; temptation of the easy sacrifice.

chapters.title: Corvane at the Broken Stone
chapters.summary: POV alternating Orsen and Corvane. Corvane catches up at the Broken Stone, but she is no simple agent: her own sister was consumed by the covenant's collapse, and she wants it reforged too—if on the crown's terms, binding the Wood as property. Sable Vey arrives with guild enforcers. Three factions converge. Emotional beat: standoff; every offer is a cage.

chapters.title: The Final Entry
chapters.summary: POV Orsen. Climax. As Sable and Corvane's forces clash, Orsen opens their own ledger before the Broken Stone and reads aloud every debt the guild ever recorded—including Sable's original crime—making truth itself the witness the oath requires. Then Orsen signs the last line with their immunity, surrendering the poison-tolerance that defines them. Emotional beat: costly resolve; justice outside any law, paid personally.

chapters.title: Where the Wood Stops Weeping
chapters.summary: POV Orsen, epilogue-like. The covenant holds; the Wood's weeping ceases, and memory flows back across both realms, including to Orsen, now ordinary and vulnerable for the first time. Sable faces the guild's own tribunal; Corvane chooses silence over a report. Orsen closes the ledger, leaves the cellar shrine empty, and walks into the city visible at last. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
